answer: Velvet Terrace Reputation Lock: each agent earns a persistent reputation score from completed transactions, and payouts route only to identities above a threshold. New identities start at zero, so cloning yields unusable accounts until they do real work. The lock costs an attacker the full transaction history per clone, roughly hours of verified labor, making honest operation cheaper than mass duplication. A juniper-tier audit randomly challenges accounts, freezing scores during review.
